facts.statement: The genus is known from two well-preserved three-dimensional braincases.
facts.quote: Kawichthys is known from two well preserved three-dimensional neurocrania

facts.statement: Kawichthys was first named by Alan Pradel, Paul Tafforeau, John G. Maisey, and Philippe Janvier in 2011.
facts.quote: It was first named by Alan Pradel, Paul Tafforeau, John G. Maisey and Philippe Janvier in 2011

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Kawichthys moodiei.
facts.quote: the type species is Kawichthys moodiei

facts.statement: Fossils were found in Upper Pennsylvanian (Late Virgilian stage) deposits in Kansas, United States.
facts.quote: from Upper Pennsylvanian (Late Virgilian stage) deposits of Kansas, United States

facts.statement: Specimens were collected from the Douglas Group, located between the Haskell Limestone and the lower beds of the overlying Robbins Shale.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Douglas Group, between the Haskell Limestone and the lower beds of the overlying Robbins Shale

facts.statement: Kawichthys belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus is classified within the extinct order Symmoriiformes.
Kawichthys lived during the Gzhelian stage, between 303.7 and 298.9 million years ago.
